title: While FIFA Counts Goals, Mexicans Count the Disappeared
author: Tamara Pearson
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/06/worldcupprotestposter.jpeg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/06/12/while-
fifa-counts-goals-mexicans-count-the-disappeared/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/06/worldcupprotestposter.jpeg)

"Behind the Cup, graves and troops are hidden," reads this placard, at a
political action in Mexico City. Photo by Tamara Pearson.

From teachers to the mothers searching for the forcibly disappeared, Mexico
will be holding numerous, massive protests against the 2026 Men's World Cup as
it kicks off in Mexico City on Thursday. This follows hundreds of protests and
actions held over the past months as FIFA and governments prioritize tourists
and corporations over urgent local needs and the environment.

The scoreboard and fouls:

**Take FIFA to forget that there is empire** - The World Cup, being held in
Mexico, the US, and Canada, will “unite the people,”
[said](https://publications.fifa.com/en/annual-report-2022/2022-at-a-
glance/fifa-world-cup-2026-host-city-announcement/) Canadian soccer player,
Jonatha Osorio. “The world will be invading Canada, Mexico and the USA with a
big wave of joy and happiness,”
[said](https://publications.fifa.com/en/annual-report-2022/2022-at-a-
glance/fifa-world-cup-2026-host-city-announcement/) FIFA president Gianni
Infantino, on a glitzy summer's evening in New York.

The same countries are also currently holding talks to renew the USMCA North
American free trade agreement for another 16 years. The USMCA, an update to
the NAFTA, is codified empire, depriving Mexico of corn sovereignty,
institutionalizing the US's dominance and Mexico's structural and economic
dependence, while sacrificing Mexico's rivers and soil to US and Canadian
mines.

The giddy glamour of the World Cup spectacle is not unity but sedation, its
stadium lights obscuring the negotiated details of imperialism and the
unfestive realities of barbed borders, wage apartheid, and centuries of
accumulated harm.

**A corporate exploitation bonanza** - The soccer ball is the pretext. The
World Cup is actually a giant advertising campaign -- experiential marketing
designed to drive sales for the corporate sponsors and move mass amounts of
merchandise.

Behind those sales there is extreme exploitation. Adidas and the company
Someone Somewhere paid 150 Indigenous Nahua embroiderers in Naupan, Puebla,
[36 pesos](https://www.diariocambio.com.mx/2026/mundial-2026/adidas-exploto-a-
las-artesanas-de-naupan-les-pago-36-pesos-la-hora-y-el-jersey-cuesta-4-mil/)
(US$2) an hour to hand-stitch the Mexico World Cup jersey — which Adidas then
sold for 4,000 pesos. Diario Cambio reported that the women were also forced
to abandon their traditional sewing techniques and use French knots and zigzag
stitching instead to fill in commercial logos -- a sidelining of cultural
knowledge. The companies also promised the workers social security, in order
to justify their "fair trade" branding (and pricing), but never kept the
promise.

And while World Cup merchandise floods Mexico's street stalls and shops, an
estimated
[70%](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/05/06/economia/mundial-de-
futbol-acelerara-el-consumo-en-mexico-canaco-preve-derrama-
de-26-mil-280-mdp%20strong%20link%20between%20television,%20junk%20food,%20and%20profits.)
of Mexicans will watch the matches on television, with a corresponding
increase in junk food purchases to go with that. Inside statidums, FIFA has
[prohibited](https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/50ebae81c412b7d5/original/FIFA-
World-Cup-2026-Stadium-Code-of-Conduct.pdf) the use of reusable water bottles
in the three host countries, meaning spectators must buy water or soft drinks,
generating huge amounts of rubbish as well as profits for corporations.

**Coca Cup** : The Cup trophy arrived in a Coca-Cola
[plane](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DVRHwXlDpdC/) at Mexico City's airport
in late February. The Mexican government rolled out the red carpet, with
foreign affairs secretary Juan Ramón de la Fuente
[receiving](https://kaosenlared.net/el-mundo-del-espectaculo-la-copa-cola-
fifa-coca-cola-y-gobierno-mexicano-un-coctel-de-despojo-y-corrupcion/) the
corporation and the trophy as though they were fellow officials. The trophy
and massive Coca-Cola boards then toured the country, including a photo shoot
at the sacred and world heritage site, [Chichén
Itza](https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2026/5/6/no-se-cometio-ninguna-
falta-por-fotos-de-la-copa-del-mundo-en-chinchen-itza-inah-373541.html) and an
[appearance](https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2026/3/3/sheinbaum-recibe-la-
copa-fifa-100-dias-del-mundial-2026-369542.html) on the president's daily news
show.

Coca-Cola has had advertising at every FIFA tournament since
[1950](https://inside.fifa.com/tournament-organisation/partners/coca-cola).
The promotions and sponsorship are a major part of its strategy to increase
consumption during the games, and for acquiring new customers. Coca-Cola,
along with companies like Pepsi and Nestle extract (steal) over [133
billion](https://www.counterpunch.org/2022/03/21/the-horrific-scam-that-water-
billionaires-are-running-on-poor-countries/) liters of Mexico's water
annually, and Mexico is already the
[biggest](https://www.mexicodesconocido.com.mx/la-region-donde-toman-mas-coca-
cola-en-el-mundo-esta-en-mexico.html) consumer of Coca-Cola globally, at an
average of 163 liters of soft drink per person per year. The FIFA-Coca-Cola
alliance is spoon-feeding more empire to a country it is already slowly
poisoning.

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/06/DSC04604-680x450.jpg)

"Behind the Cup, graves and troops are hidden," reads this placard, at a
political action in Mexico City. Photo by Tamara Pearson.

**Red carpet for tourists, disposable locals - **The US and Mexico are
employing selective hospitality for the World Cup -- or, more precisely,
implementing racist and classist measures of city beautification for some, and
social cleansing, deportations, raids, repression, and evictions for others.

The US is [promoting](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-
actions/2025/03/establishing-the-white-house-task-force-on-the-fifa-world-
cup-2026/%20ironic%20considering%20treatement%20of%20migrants) the World Cup
as a way to "showcase" their "hospitality," while simultaneously violating a
range of human rights with its closed border, ICE racial profiling, and
illegal and cruel deportations.

In Mexico City over the past month, officials have also held anti-migrant
[raids](https://redtdt.org.mx/archivos/23648), where police, the military, and
migration authorities have detained people who are typically irregular
precisely because of the closed border to the north and horrific wait times
and unfair outcomes from Mexican institutions. Social cleansing for the World
Cup also includes removing [vendors](https://desinformemonos.org/gobierno-de-
ciudad-de-mexico-congela-dialogo-con-comunidades-afectadas-por-el-
mundial-2026/) from the area near the Mexico City stadium and
[homeless](https://grupoanimal.mx/sociedad/poblaciones-callejeras-denuncian-
limpieza-social-mudial) people from parts of the city where tourists are
expected. Sex workers report that a new 17-kilometer [bike
lane](https://www.lavozdemichoacan.com.mx/mexico/cdmx/protesta-ciclovia-
tlalpan-mundial-2026-limpieza-social-cdmx/) built for the World Cup has left
thousands of them without work, and local communities, who weren't consulted,
said they support bike lanes, but this one cuts through bus stops, endangering
pedestrians.

The government is also valuing Mexico's beautiful axolotls more as World Cup
mascots, than living creatures. It spent 62 million pesos
[adorning](https://www.obras.cdmx.gob.mx/comunicacion/nota/entrega-clara-
brugada-modernizacion-del-tren-ligero-el-ajolote) walls around the city and
the light-rail with axolotl images, while nearby in Xochimilco, the animals
are endangered due to contaminated runoff and public
[works](https://medioambiente.nexos.com.mx/un-puente-vehicular-devasta-el-
humedal-de-xochimilco/).

Further, the government is staging Day of the Dead celebrations in
[June](https://vanguardia.com.mx/noticias/mexico/dia-de-muertos-en-junio-por-
el-mundial-en-cdmx-preparan-desfile-y-colocan-flores-de-cempasuchil-
BE21161819) just for tourists, while erecting massive metal perimeters around
Mexico City's main [square](https://www.facebook.com/share/1E4TsAbv2o/). There
is a two-kilometer exclusion [zone](https://grupoanimal.mx/verificacion-de-
hechos/como-funcionara-operativo-ultima-milla-estadio-banorte-mundial-cdmx)
around the stadium that is causing huge difficulties for locals as well as
stopping protesters and protecting the tourists and wealthy who can afford
expensive stadium seats.

**Street soccer** - "The streets are our soccer fields, and we assert our
right to the city, to protest, and to freedom of assembly,"
[said](https://www.somoselmedio.com/asamblea-comun-contra-guerra-jornadas-
antimundialistas-cdmx/) members of the Assembly for the Common Good and
Against the War. And indeed, billions of dollars and corporate sponsorships
aren't necessary for sport or fun. Known as cascaritas in Mexico -- and by
other names around Latin America and much of the Global South -- informal and
improvised soccer games played in parks, parking lots, and in the streets, can
be easy, free, and truly inclusive.

This soccer is played with a few backpacks or empty water jugs as goal posts,
a hand-painted or chalk-drawn court, and an empty can or an old plastic ball.
The name, cascaritas, comes from orange peal, because even an orange can be a
ball -- though it will eventually become quite beaten up and the peal will
come off. When the objective is to have fun, any genders and ages can join in,
only a few basic rules are followed, and even those watching are more
involved, as they are the neighbors and friends of the players.

**Protest, organizing, and community is what actually brings people together**
- Over the past few months, movements and collectives around Mexico have held
hundreds of events protesting the World Cup and its direct impact, as well as
using it to draw attention to the reality in the country, and beyond.

People have held soccer against
[genocide](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/futbol-contra-el-
genocidio-en-santo-domingo-concluye-torneo-intifada-antififa/) and for
Palestine, [feminist](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/gana-una-
ganamos-todas-quinta-edicion-de-las-retas-feministas-en-cdmx-durante-el-paro-
de-mujeres/) soccer, soccer matches against the
[looting](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/retas-anti-fifa-apropiarse-
del-futbol-para-defender-el-territorio/) of water and against gentrification
with Trump's head as a ball, soccer in San Pedro Xolostoc to promote
[community](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/cancha-violeta-el-futbol-
barrial-que-teje-comunidad-en-san-pedro-xalostoc/)building, and soccer matches
against a rubbish [dump](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/ganamos-
porque-ya-estamos-jugando-el-futbol-en-la-resistencia-contra-el-basurero-en-
cholula/) on Indigenous lands. In
[Jalisco](https://www.zonadocs.mx/2026/05/18/festival-anti-mundialista-una-
protesta-contra-el-gasto-excesivo-del-mundial/), collectives held an Anti-
World Cup People's Cascarita to denounce that while the state and national
governments prepare for the World Cup, they aren't doing anything about the
water crisis, housing, and disappearances. Various groups stood in front of
the World Cup Watch to [announce](https://www.somoselmedio.com/asamblea-comun-
contra-guerra-jornadas-antimundialistas-cdmx/) the formation of an Assembly
for the Common Good and a series of anti-World Cup actions. And of course
there have been
[countless](https://www.facebook.com/RebeldiasResistenciasElComunYOtrasLuchas/posts/pfbid02cFkrujL5mDx6PMTefuXEaZ1ewagPxGUoeGJ3KzSjoioos85rLHkBfz3CU6KPYyngl)
[actions](https://www.facebook.com/ElUniversalOnline/posts/pfbid02X7iqoR22QBssU2iHU4kDqBrwAquoQ3Yu2Q1WkjnGxVjGruQvtgWVwazVHYpLshDEl)
for the forcibly disappeared, and the massive education worker strikes and
marches - mentioned below.

For Thursday, families looking for the forcibly disappeared have
[called](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/mientras-adentro-celebran-
afuera-lloramos-familias-en-busqueda-lanzan-llamado-a-manifestacion-nacional-
en-la-inauguracion-del-mundial-2026/) for a national protest, and will be
[joined](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/alistan-mega-marcha-para-
inauguracion-del-mundial-en-cdmx-este-11-de-junio-conoce-los-detalles-y-
cierres-viales/) by teachers, retirees, transport workers, small farmers,
healthcare workers, and other movements. Already, participants in this protest
have faced problems, with a contingent of [17
buses](https://oem.com.mx/elsoldeacapulco/mexico/a-bordo-de-17-autobuses-
retenidos-normalistas-se-suman-a-movilizaciones-en-cdmx-30430413) from
Guerrero state of student teachers and parents of the 43 Ayotzinapa students
that were forcibly disappeared, being
[stopped](https://www.facebook.com/watch/live/?ref=watch_permalink&v=1314749840781941)
by [police](http://facebook.com/reel/1297639645873773/) from reaching Mexico
City, Monday.

"The ball is coming home, when will they?" activists
[painted](https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/justicia/2026/5/17/la-pelota-
vuelve-casa-ellxs-cuando-nueva-protesta-de-colectivos-en-paseo-de-la-
reforma-374215.html) in massive letters on the road in Mexico City, in front
of a wall of posters for the 133,00 forcibly disappeared. Our goals are bigger
than getting a ball in net. We want justice, and the day Mexico has that,
there will truly be something to celebrate.

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/06/worldcuptrain-680x470.png)

The government has adorned the light rail train with Axolotls for the World
Cup, while the animal itself lacks care and protection. Photo by Tamara
Pearson.

**Safety for the World Cup, but not for women, Indigenous communities,
activists, or journalists**. -- Mexico announced that it will deploy almost
[100,000](https://www.france24.com/es/minuto-a-minuto/20260309-m%C3%A9xico-
desplegar%C3%A1-casi-100-000-efectivos-de-seguridad-para-el-mundial) security
forces (including police, military, and private security) to the three cities
hosting the world cup. The national government also
[approved](https://www.espn.com.mx/futbol/mundial/nota/_/id/16484081/mundial-2026-mexico-
ingreso-soldados-estados-unidos-adiestramiento) US Armed Forces entry into the
country, to train and prepare Mexican forces for the World Cup. Meanwhile, no
such resources are deployed to prevent or solve femicides - with an impunity
rate of [95%](https://grupoanimal.mx/sociedad/mexico-feminicidios-disfrazados-
impunidad-casos), nor to clean our dead rivers, monitor workplace abuses, and
so on.

**Students and educators come last** -- The Mexican government initially
announced a massive three-month-long school
[holiday](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/no-es-una-medida-
pedagogica-sino-politica-cnte-critica-recorte-de-clases-por-el-mundial/) to
accommodate the World Cup schedule, by bringing forward the usual holidays by
six weeks. Many teachers are only paid for classroom hours and struggle during
holidays, while parents and carers would have had to seek childcare, and
children would have missed out on significant learning. After much criticism,
the measure was [retracted](https://grupoanimal.mx/sociedad/sep-ciclo-escolar-
este-dia-terminan-clases/).

Teachers have also gone on strike and threatened to
[stop](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/no-es-metafora-decir-que-si-
no-hay-solucion-no-rodara-el-balon-cnte-ante-incumplimiento-de-demandas/) the
World Cup, holding protests, marches, road blocks, and more since mid May to
demand pension rights, among other worker rights, which President Sheinbaum
promised in her campaign but hasn't delivered. Instead, these protests have
been blocked with hundreds of police and
[repressed](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/06/01/politica/cnte-
determina-instalar-planton-en-20-de-noviembre-al-no-poder-ingresar-al-
zocalo)with tear gas and rubber bullets, with one teacher losing his left eye
and sight in the other, as a result. Protesting teachers used rope to
[tumble](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/06/02/politica/presuntos-
integrantes-de-la-cnte-derriban-tres-de-las-estatuas-de-futbolistas-
instaladas-en-reforma) three giant statues of soccer players that the
government had erected on a key road in Mexico City.

**Complicit venues** - The venue in Mexico City, Azteca Stadium (technically
called Banorte), the largest in Latin America, is owned by Televisa via Grupo
Ollamani. Last year, the government granted Televisa a water concession next
to the stadium for [450
million](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/exigen-expropiacion-del-
pozo-de-televisa-y-donde-haya-inversion-publica-para-el-mundial-en-ciudad-de-
mexico/) liters a year - thereby
[illegally](https://fueradelugar.desinformemonos.org/televisa-especula-con-su-
concesion-de-agua-para-el-estadio-azteca/) privatizing local public water, and
causing water shortages for those nearby. Not only does Televisa own the
stadium, but it and TV Azteca are the companies with
[transmission](https://alfilo.lat/fut/la-cascarita/mundial-2026-tv-azteca-
televisa-costo/) rights.

In Guadalajara, clandestine mass
[graves](https://elpais.com/mexico/2026-05-20/guadalajara-se-enfrenta-al-
legado-de-la-violencia-de-los-carteles-en-medio-del-entusiasmo-por-el-
mundial.html) have been found near the Akron Stadium, where four matches will
be played. In Guadalajara too, the government is employing heavy machinery to
renovate and clean up the city in preparation for the World Cup, but there is
no digging equipment available to help searchers find the thousands of
forcibly disappeared.

Disappeared](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/06/12/while-fifa-counts-goals-
mexicans-count-the-disappeared/) appeared first on
[CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
